transcript.text: You mentioned managing a team of 12 at a fulfilment centre handling 8,000 orders a day. Can you describe your key challenges and approaches in this role?

I worked for seven years in e-commerce logistics in Pune, finishing as operations lead managing a team of 12 at a fulfilment centre that handled 8,000 orders a day. I brought the order-to-dispatch time down from 26 hours to 19. Then I took a two-year break from work, and I completed a supply-chain analytics course in 2024 to keep learning. I'm applying now to return at a higher level, because I want to design the supply network and not only run one site.
How did your leadership help in reducing the order-to-dispatch time from 26 hours to 19 hours?
transcript.anchor_quote: I brought the order-to-dispatch time down from 26 hours to 19

transcript.text: To cut the dispatch time I changed the pick-path in the warehouse. Fast-moving items were moved closer to the packing area. Packers were also asked to start the day with the oldest orders. That solved most of the delay in the afternoon batch.
What specific challenges did you face when redesigning the pick-path and order prioritization, and how did you decide on these particular changes?
transcript.anchor_quote: To cut the dispatch time I changed the pick-path in the warehouse. Fast-moving items were moved closer to the packing area

transcript.text: The break helped me reflect and recharge. I have emerged with a fresh perspective and I am more motivated than ever to create impact in the next phase of my journey.

feedback.summary: The candidate has relevant e-commerce operations experience and demonstrates understanding of supply-chain concepts and process improvements. However, there is a key inconsistency in their description of managerial responsibilities that requires clarification. The candidate effectively explained a process improvement to reduce dispatch time, but struggles to connect recent learning to practical application and did not provide substantiated outcomes from their initiatives. Motivation for pursuing an MBA is broadly stated but lacks detail about specific career goals and how the MBA fits into them. Contributions to peers and learning from setbacks remain untested.
